title: Polaris Sprints
subtitle: Execution governance and 90-day sprint architecture — answering one question per cycle: what must be true in 90 days to de-risk the next stage, and how do we get there?

sections.heading: Performance Governance That Connects Operations to Capital Decisions
sections.body:
Polaris Sprints translate strategic intent into a measurable, board-level performance dashboard — connecting sales, delivery and governance work directly to capital allocation decisions. Every metric is chosen because it drives a specific governance decision, not because it is easy to collect.

+++ The seven metrics on the dashboard

CUSTOMER PROFITABILITY — Does each customer bring in substantially more over its lifetime than it costs to win? Below the minimum threshold, growth destroys value.

ACQUISITION PAYBACK — How long does it take to earn back the cost of winning a customer? With institutional sales cycles of six to eighteen months, this decides how much runway a sale consumes.

PROCUREMENT PASS RATE — Of the deals that reach security and compliance review, how many get through, and where do the others stop?

TIME TO GO-LIVE — How long from signed contract to a customer in production? In regulated markets, a slow or failed onboarding costs trust that is hard to win back.

CASH FLOW SUSTAINABILITY — Is the business generating enough operating cash to sustain itself without constant external capital?

LIQUIDITY AND RUNWAY — Can the business meet its near-term obligations, and for how many months? Below the minimum threshold, this is an immediate 6Sense Risk flag.

GOVERNANCE MATURITY — The AI Compass score, measured again at the end of every sprint.

sections.heading: Hybrid Agile Execution — Not One Size Fits All
sections.body:
Polaris 90-day sprints combine high-velocity Scrum and Kanban cycles for product development with gated milestone patterns for regulatory governance. Teams iterate rapidly while maintaining full auditability — which is non-negotiable in regulated sectors.

Each sprint produces evidence, not features. The output is a validated or falsified hypothesis that changes the capital-commitment decision for the next stage.

> Compliance and product development are synchronised through explicit handover checkpoints — ensuring that regulatory gate-passes and product iterations move together, not in parallel silos that collide at the worst possible moment.

sections.heading: Capital Velocity and Bottleneck Removal
sections.body:
Each 90-day sprint targets the single most limiting constraint in the system — the bottleneck that, if removed, creates the most forward momentum. Lead times shrink. Cash moves faster. The path to market becomes shorter.

Sprint design begins with one question: where is the highest-bandwidth feedback environment available to test the critical hypothesis? Validation happens there first — before capital is committed to scale.

sections.heading: How AI Gains Are Counted
sections.body:
Every sprint that deploys AI states in advance how the gain will be taken out: as capacity, as quality, or as cost. Capacity and quality are assessed first.

A gain that is only counted in headcount is the easiest to measure and often the least valuable.

sections.heading: Knowledge That Survives the Sprint
sections.body:
Every Polaris sprint that deploys new capability into a company includes the design of an internal champion network — a super-user layer that ensures knowledge survives the sprint team's exit.

Capability that lives only in the deploying team evaporates when the engagement ends. The champion network converts sprint outcomes into durable organisational change — and it is designed before the sprint begins, not retrofitted at the end.
